rule.title: Potential Sidecar Injection Into Running Deployment
rule.author: Leo Tsaousis (@laripping)

es.summary: Una identidad envió una solicitud PATCH sobre un Deployment del grupo de API apps. Puede ser un cambio rutinario o la inyección de un contenedor sidecar para ejecutar código oculto dentro de una carga de trabajo legítima.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de auditoría de Kubernetes con verb 'patch', apiGroup 'apps' y objectRef.resource 'deployments'. La regla coincide con cualquier patch a un Deployment, no solo con los que agregan un contenedor, así que hay que revisar el cuerpo de la solicitud.
es.why_it_matters: Un atacante que agrega un sidecar a un Deployment existente ejecuta código con la service account, el acceso de red y los secretos montados del pod, y se camufla entre pods legítimos. Corresponde a ATT&CK T1609, Container Administration Command (Ejecución).
triage_steps: Registre user.username, user.groups, sourceIPs, userAgent, objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name y responseStatus.code. Verifique si el patch se aplicó.
Si se registra requestObject, revise si spec.template.spec.containers o initContainers tienen una entrada nueva. Anote la imagen, el comando, los volúmenes montados y el securityContext.
Compare las revisiones de ReplicaSet con 'kubectl rollout history deployment/<nombre> -n <ns> --revision=N' para ver el cambio real del spec.
Confirme si la identidad es una cuenta conocida de CI/CD o GitOps (Argo CD, Flux, Helm) y si su userAgent e IP de origen coinciden con su patrón habitual.
Busque actividad del mismo usuario e IP de origen en +/- 15 minutos: lectura de secrets, pods/exec, cambios de RBAC o service accounts nuevas.
Confirme con el responsable de la carga de trabajo si hay un ticket de cambio o un pull request aprobado que coincida con la hora.
Valide el registry y el digest de la imagen nueva contra los registries aprobados, y revise el tráfico de salida de los pods nuevos.
false_positives: Pipelines de CI/CD, upgrades de Helm o controladores GitOps que aplican patch a Deployments durante despliegues normales.
'kubectl rollout restart', 'kubectl set image' o escalados, que generan patch sin agregar contenedores.
Administradores que agregan sidecars aprobados de logging, proxy o monitoreo, o anotaciones para la inyección del service mesh.
response_steps: Verifique con el responsable. Si el cambio no está autorizado, conserve los eventos de auditoría y el manifiesto actual del Deployment como evidencia.
Revierta con 'kubectl rollout undo' a la última revisión confiable, o escale el Deployment a cero si el código inyectado está activo.
Revoque o rote las credenciales o el token que hizo el patch, y también los secretos accesibles desde los pods afectados.
Revise el RBAC para que solo las identidades previstas puedan hacer patch a Deployments. Evalúe políticas de admisión que restrinjan imágenes y contenedores.
Busque patches similares en otros Deployments, DaemonSets y StatefulSets, y bloquee la imagen inyectada.
es.severity_rationale: La severidad media es adecuada porque un sidecar no autorizado da ejecución sigilosa, pero los patch a Deployments son frecuentes en la operación normal y requieren contexto para confirmarse.

en.summary: A principal sent a PATCH request against a Deployment in the apps API group. This may be a routine change, or someone injecting a sidecar container to run hidden code inside a legitimate workload.
en.what_it_detects: Kubernetes audit events where verb is 'patch', apiGroup is 'apps' and objectRef.resource is 'deployments'. The rule matches every patch to a Deployment, not only ones that add a container, so the request body needs review.
en.why_it_matters: An attacker who adds a sidecar to an existing Deployment can run code with the pod's service account, network access and mounted secrets, and blends in with legitimate pods. This maps to ATT&CK T1609, Container Administration Command (Execution).
triage_steps: Record user.username, user.groups, sourceIPs, userAgent, objectRef.namespace, objectRef.name and responseStatus.code. Check whether the patch succeeded.
If requestObject is logged, check whether spec.template.spec.containers or initContainers gained an entry. Note the new image, command, volume mounts and securityContext.
Compare ReplicaSet revisions with 'kubectl rollout history deployment/<name> -n <ns> --revision=N' to see the actual spec change.
Check whether the identity is a known CI/CD or GitOps account (Argo CD, Flux, Helm) and whether its userAgent and source IP match its usual pattern.
Pivot on the same user and source IP within +/- 15 minutes for secrets reads, pods/exec, RBAC changes or new service accounts.
Confirm with the workload owner whether a change ticket or merged pull request matches the timestamp.
Check the new image's registry and digest against approved registries, and look at egress from the new pods.
false_positives: CI/CD pipelines, Helm upgrades or GitOps controllers patching Deployments during normal releases.
'kubectl rollout restart', 'kubectl set image' or scaling, which issue patch requests without adding containers.
Administrators adding approved logging, proxy or monitoring sidecars, or annotations for service-mesh injection.
response_steps: Verify with the owner. If the change is unauthorized, preserve the audit events and the current Deployment manifest as evidence.
Roll back with 'kubectl rollout undo' to the last known-good revision, or scale the Deployment to zero if the injected code is active.
Revoke or rotate the credentials or token that made the patch, plus any secrets the affected pods could reach.
Review RBAC so only intended identities can patch Deployments. Consider admission policies that restrict images and containers.
Hunt for similar patches to other Deployments, DaemonSets and StatefulSets, and block the injected image.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits because unauthorized sidecars give stealthy code execution, but Deployment patches are common in normal operations and need context to confirm.

positive.description: An unknown user patches a production Deployment with kubectl to add a sidecar container.
A service account patches a Deployment through a client library from an internal IP.

negative.description: A patch to a DaemonSet in the apps group. Its resource is not deployments.
A read-only get of a Deployment. The verb is not patch.
